resource.name: Mission / Vision / Strategy Alignment Checker
resource.description: Paste mission, vision, and current quarter's strategy doc. Surfaces drift between the three, platitudes, operational gaps in named bets, and a Rumelt diagnosis of the strategy.

tools.name: alignment_drift_map
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Three pairwise comparisons (mission-vs-vision, mission-vs-strategy, vision-vs-strategy) with drift severity and a 10-word drift label per pair.

tools.name: alignment_platitude_detector
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Lists empty phrases in each doc, verbatim, with what each would have to say to be load-bearing.

custom_phrases.description: Optional team-specific platitudes to add to the base detection list.

tools.name: alignment_operational_gaps
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Extracts named bets from the strategy and produces the questions the user should ask team leads to test operational follow-through. In Phase 1, output is questions. In Phase 2 with roadmap files, output is assertions.

team_roadmaps.description: Phase 2 only. .mcpb bundle populates this array from local roadmap files. Phase 1 omits the array.

operational_assertion.description: Phase 2 only. Omitted in Phase 1 output where only operational_question is populated.

tools.name: alignment_rumelt_diagnosis
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Direct application of Rumelt's diagnosis test to the strategy doc only.

named_challenge.description: Optional. Omitted when the strategy names no real challenge.

guiding_policy.description: Optional. Omitted when no guiding policy is identifiable.

tools.name: alignment_quarterly_diff
tools.description: MCP-only (stateful). Compares this quarter's mission/vision/strategy against last quarter's. Surfaces drift direction (did the strategy drift away from the mission, or did the mission drift to follow the strategy?). Stores quarterly triples locally across runs.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.phase_note: Web version does not expose this. Quarterly diff requires persisted prior triples in the .mcpb bundle's data dir; host's confirmation UI handles the consent surface.

tools.name: alignment_board_prep
tools.description: MCP-only. Outputs a one-page board pre-read artifact (Markdown) summarizing the drift map, Rumelt verdict, and the three highest-leverage operational gaps. Reads from persisted quarterly triples.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.phase_note: Reads the persisted triples from alignment_quarterly_diff; same data-dir scope.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.comment: MCP resource spec for #47 Mission/Vision/Strategy Alignment Checker. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. Validated against MCP Apps spec (Jan 2026 release + current draft) on 2026-05-18.

dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.summary: Narration tools in this app return a narration_brief, not the structured prose directly. The outputSchema(s) defined above describe the target rendering structure the host chat model is asked to produce. At runtime each narration tool returns { type: 'narration_brief', audience: 'user', directive, voice_rules, structure: { sections, per_section_template, length_cap }, inputs: <tool-specific>, corpus: { anchor_slug: chunk_text } }. The host chat model then renders the user-facing prose from the brief.
dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.worked_example: bundle/src/tools/pm-pitfalls/narrate.ts and bundle/src/shared/schemas.ts (PitfallNarrateOutput). Sonnet clones this pattern for every narration tool listed below.
dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.supersedes: Earlier 'host sampling + api_key fallback' design. Sampling/createMessage was not exposed by Claude Desktop or Claude Code CLI to user-installed extensions in 2026-05; Path 4 makes the host chat model the renderer, which is the MCP-recommended idiom.

dev.workingfromlenny.open_questions: Drift-map visualization: in Phase 1 web, render the three-box arrow diagram as inline SVG or as CSS-grid blocks? Inline SVG scales; CSS-grid is lighter.
Platitude detector: should the list of flagged phrase patterns be user-editable (a team's actual platitudes vary), or locked? Locked is simpler but misses team-specific jargon.
Board-prep tool: should the output be Markdown, PDF, or a structured JSON the user converts? PDF requires a Worker dependency; Markdown is most flexible.
dev.workingfromlenny.proposed_answers: Inline SVG for the drift-map visualization. The three-box diagram has semantic content (drift direction, severity) that CSS-grid cannot encode without custom classes. Inline SVG scales to card width, allows color-coding arrows by severity (none/low/med/high with a four-color scale), and renders without an external dependency. Note: this answers the HTML build question gated on owner sign-off per PROCEDURAL_REFERENCE.md; no code change made here.

Lock the base pattern list; add a custom_phrases optional array to the inputSchema for team-specific overrides (now applied above on alignment_platitude_detector). This gives teams a lightweight escape hatch per-run without opening the base list to per-user configuration that would complicate corpus maintenance.

Markdown output for Phase 2 (now applied — alignment_board_prep emits Markdown). PDF would require a headless rendering dependency (Puppeteer or a Worker with wasm) that is out of scope for the .mcpb bundle format. Structured JSON shifts formatting burden to the user. Markdown is immediately usable in Notion, Linear, or a Google Doc paste, which is where board pre-reads actually live.
_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.outputSchema_refact: Removed `type: ['string', 'null']` on operational_assertion, named_challenge, and guiding_policy; changed to plain optional strings. Absent fields are unambiguous in the MCP output contract.

notes: ui:// scheme is valid; no rigid format is enforced — server-defined slugs after the scheme are acceptable.

No requires-consent / data-retention / fs-write capability exists in either ext-apps appCapabilities or .mcpb manifest. Consent is host-discretion; readOnlyHint: false on stateful tools is the only normative hook.
Underscore-prefixed fields at non-_meta paths have undefined host behavior; project metadata lives under _meta with reverse-DNS keys.
